import_provenance.original_title: Automatic iterative learning versus hypothesis-sized memory
import_provenance.original_statement: Does allowing an automatic learner additional memory bounded by the length of its current hypothesis strictly increase what it can identify in the limit from positive data, compared with retaining only the previous hypothesis? Compare learnable automatic families allowing suitable automatic hypothesis-space recodings, rather than fixing a potentially restrictive original indexing.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The question concerns positive examples without a counterexample oracle. The 2017 paper already proves iterative learning of automatic families consisting only of infinite languages when bounded negative counterexamples are supplied.
